name: Digital Realty Trust, Inc.
employees: 4,282 full-time (31 December 2025) — 1,948 North America, 2,040 EMEA, 294 Asia Pacific
summary:
**BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:** Digital Realty is the largest listed wholesale data-centre landlord by leasable area and development pipeline — 310 data centres, approximately 3.1 GW of in-place IT capacity and approximately 8.5 GW buildable at 30 June 2026 — but it is the second-largest listed data-centre REIT by revenue and market value behind Equinix, and the proposition that it leads an 'AI landlord' market is **unfalsifiable rather than true or false**: no published ranking measures AI-attributable landlord capacity, and the sponsor-owned platforms a January 2026 Bank of America downgrade identified as capturing that demand disclose nothing comparable. The company's own superlative is always narrowed to 'cloud- and carrier-neutral' and is never attributed to a third party. Two things inflected in 2026: capacity under development rose 82% in six months to 1,402 MW while the pre-leased share of it fell from 64% to 54%, and the cash mark-to-market on renewals reached 25.4% on a greater-than-1 MW book repricing at 66.7% — with 25.9% of annualised rent expiring in 2026 alone.

**BACKGROUND.** Maryland real estate investment trust incorporated 9 March 2004, listed as NYSE: DLR, with the operating partnership Digital Realty Trust, L.P. organised 21 July 2004; headquarters 601 W. 2nd Street, Austin, Texas; 4,282 full-time employees at 31 December 2025, a majority of them in EMEA (2,040 against 1,948 in North America) — the demographic residue of the Interxion combination. FY2025 revenue USD 6,112.7m (+10.0%), net income available to common stockholders USD 1,267.9m, Core FFO USD 7.39 a share, Adjusted EBITDA about USD 3.34bn, per SEC filings. Customer concentration is high and partly undisclosed: the twenty largest customers are 50.9% of annualised recurring revenue and the top three are approximately 26%, while the largest single customer at 11.7% is identified in the 10-K only as a 'Fortune 50 Software Company'. The platform was assembled by acquisition — Telx (2015), DuPont Fabros (2017), Ascenty (2018), Interxion (2020) and a 55% interest in Teraco (2022, raised to 77% in June 2026) — and the company now states three growth pillars: colocation and connectivity, hyperscale, and strategic private capital, the third running USD 190.2m of annualised net development and management fees.
ecosystemRole: The listed benchmark for what a data-centre landlord is worth and how one is financed. Digital Realty sits on the landlord side of this corpus alongside Equinix, QTS, Vantage, Aligned, STACK, Compass, EdgeCore and CyrusOne, and is the one whose economics are fully public: a REIT that must distribute most of its taxable income and therefore funds a USD 4.25-4.75bn annual development programme from equity issuance, unsecured notes and — increasingly — third-party capital it manages for a fee. That third channel is the strategically live part: a USD 3.25bn US hyperscale fund closed in March 2026 with Digital Realty retaining 20% and the management mandate, twenty unconsolidated joint ventures, and fee income that nearly doubled year on year. For the equipment suppliers in this corpus it is a named buyer under a USD 373m Schneider Electric supply-capacity agreement; for the power side it is an energy-services counterparty in Kansas and a PPA buyer in Europe; and for the private landlords it is the public comparable their sponsors are implicitly marked against.

productsAndServices.name: Colocation — data centre services, suites and High-Density Colocation
productsAndServices.description: The retail-to-scale end of the platform, sold under the PlatformDIGITAL banner. Turn-Key Flex pre-commissioned suites in a distributed-redundant design that can be subdivided; Data Center Services covering on-demand and scheduled remote work (tape swaps, hard and soft reboots, patch-cord installation, equipment transport, KVM output, cross-connect loopback verification, rack-and-stack and structured cabling, maintenance-window support) with more than ten services offered 24 hours a day, 365 days a year; and High-Density Colocation, the AI product, which the company states starts at 30 kW per cabinet and scales to multi-megawatt deployments at up to 150 kW per cabinet using Air-Assisted Liquid Cooling and Direct Liquid Cooling. The high-density page cites 170 sites across 33 markets.
highlights: High-Density Colocation: '30 kW per cabinet … scales to multi-MW sizes and up to 150 kW per cabinet' (company page); the same 30-150 kW range is repeated on the AI solutions page
Named cooling technologies are Air-Assisted Liquid Cooling (AALC) and Direct Liquid Cooling (DLC). No first-party source names rear-door heat exchangers as a product option

Two liquid-cooling proof points in 2026: the first direct liquid-cooled AI deployment in the UK with Imperial College London (2 February) and an NVIDIA certification for a liquid-cooled data centre in Japan (9 February)
0-1 MW plus interconnection was 52% of Q2 2026 bookings at USD 108m of USD 208.5m — the small-deployment book is half the sales engine, not a legacy tail
Renewal pricing splits sharply by size: 0-1 MW renewed at +5.2% cash in Q2 2026 against +66.7% for greater-than-1 MW deals
productsAndServices.positioning: The company publishes no competitor-relative positioning of any kind — no first-party page names Equinix, NTT, CyrusOne, Vantage, QTS or any other operator and argues against it. Its competitive framing is self-superlative plus third-party validation it elects to publicise, such as being named a Leader in the IDC MarketScape worldwide datacenter colocation services assessment for a fourth time (14 August 2025). Its own 10-K, by contrast, does name competitors: Equinix, NTT and Global Switch, plus unnamed US private and regional operators.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct sales alongside the unified PartnerOne programme, which carries a resell track ('compelling margins'), a referral track ('comprehensive commissions') and a separate PartnerOne Broker Programme for real-estate brokers. Named partner categories: technology services distributors, agents, referral consultants, network providers, value-added resellers, systems integrators, managed service providers and alliance partners. Cloud and technology alliances listed in the site navigation are AWS, Google Cloud, IBM Cloud, Oracle Cloud, NVIDIA, HPE GreenLake, Microsoft Azure and Dell.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: AI, data, cloud and network providers; financial services, public sector, healthcare, retail, insurance, manufacturing, transportation, media and entertainment, utilities, automotive and professional services
productsAndServices.roadmap: Singapore: selected to develop 50 MW of new capacity (25 August 2026), inside a stated near-S$7bn investment programme with more than S$4.3bn earmarked for new developments and headcount rising to 400 by 2030.

productsAndServices.name: Hyperscale and build-to-suit, including Powered Base Buildings
productsAndServices.description: Custom capacity for the largest customers. Build-to-Suit lets a customer co-design electrical, mechanical and cooling systems on a pad-ready parcel, along with entrances, truck bays and office space, with roughly 5 GW of buildable IT capacity cited as available; the pitch is avoiding the upfront cost of self-build while still getting a custom design. Powered Base Buildings are fit-out-ready shells on power- and fibre-provisioned sites, and are a reported revenue category in their own right — the supplemental defines 'Other' revenue as including Powered Base Building shell capacity alongside storage and office space, and it contributed USD 0.3m, under 1%, of Q2 2026 bookings.
highlights: 1,402 MW of projects underway at 30 June 2026 — an 82% increase in six months — of which 54% was pre-leased, down from 64% on 769 MW at 31 December 2025
Estimated pre-tax stabilised cash yield on the whole 1,402 MW is approximately 11.5% (10-Q)
More than 7 GW of additional future development capacity, roughly 70% of it in locations with more than 100 MW of buildable capacity
Two hyperscale leases signed in July 2026 alone for USD 410m at 100% share, USD 205m at Digital Realty's share
Q1 2026 carried 'the largest hyperscale lease in company history'; greater-than-1 MW bookings that quarter were about USD 325m at share
productsAndServices.positioning: No first-party competitive positioning is published. Independently, the January 2026 Bank of America downgrade argued the opposite of a leadership claim: that growth is 'constrained by the scale and location of its development pipeline, which is a poor fit for current AI driven demand', with AI capacity shifting to private operators in non-traditional locations.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct, and increasingly through managed vehicles — the US Hyperscale Data Center Fund and the joint ventures hold hyperscale assets in which Digital Realty is both minority owner and manager.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Hyperscale cloud providers, AI model developers and large enterprises taking multi-megawatt capacity
productsAndServices.roadmap: Kansas City: approximately 1,440 acres at Astra Enterprise Park, De Soto, Kansas, bought April 2026, with an energy service agreement for 600 MW by early 2028 rising to 2 GW at full delivery; the company's own community page describes Astra North as roughly 280 acres, nine buildings and about 3 million sq ft, developed in phases, and states no megawatt figure. Two Atlanta land assemblages for 1 GW-plus campuses closed in June 2026.

productsAndServices.name: Connectivity and interconnection — ServiceFabric, cross connects, DRIX and IP Bandwidth
productsAndServices.description: The network layer that distinguishes a colocation platform from a warehouse. ServiceFabric is described as a private, open virtual connectivity layer reaching 800-plus data centres and 350-plus cloud on-ramps, with a single multi-service port, a service directory and software-defined provisioning. Cross Connect is the physical meet-me-room connection ordered through the Marketplace Portal, offered at 255-plus facilities. Digital Realty Internet Exchange runs six exchanges in the United States and is pitched as a way of bypassing IP transit costs. IP Bandwidth is a dedicated multi-homed internet service at 100-plus facilities. Campus Connect and Metro Connect complete the set.
highlights: ServiceFabric MCP, launched 17 June 2026, is the platform's most substantial product event of the period: a Model Context Protocol control plane available immediately across more than 800 Digital Realty and partner-connected data centres, with intent-based connectivity provisioning, real-time capacity and topology discovery, OAuth 2 identity control and agent-assisted diagnostics integrating Slack, Microsoft Teams, Splunk and Datadog, built on patented AI Private Exchange orchestration
Interconnection contributed USD 20.5m, 10%, of Q2 2026 bookings at Digital Realty's share
Two conflicting first-party cross-connect counts are published — 230,000 on the partner-programme page and 235,500-plus on the sponsored Digital Core REIT site; neither is dated
The 800-plus figure includes partner-connected sites, not only owned ones — a scope distinction the page makes and summaries routinely drop
productsAndServices.positioning: The corpus's other dossiers place this layer second to Equinix by design: Equinix's own dossier records it as the retail-segment leader at about 17% share per Synergy and leader in 16 of the top 25 metros, with Digital Realty second in North America; QTS's dossier states that it does not compete with Equinix or Digital Realty on internet-exchange density. Digital Realty itself publishes no such comparison.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Self-service through the Marketplace Portal for cross connects, direct sales for fabric and bandwidth, and the PartnerOne channel.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Network and cloud providers, enterprises building hybrid architectures, and AI companies needing private paths between training and inference estates
productsAndServices.roadmap: No dated forward commitment is published for the connectivity line beyond the MCP launch itself.

productsAndServices.name: Strategic private capital — funds, joint ventures and fee income
productsAndServices.description: Named by the company as one of its three core pillars of growth alongside colocation and connectivity and hyperscale, and the pillar that changes what kind of business this is. Digital Realty raises third-party equity, contributes a minority stake, keeps the development and management mandate, and books a fee. The supplemental lists twenty unconsolidated entities: Ascenty, Blackstone NoVa, Clise, Digital Realty DC Partners NA Fund, GI Partners, Mapletree, Menlo, Mitsubishi, Realty Income, TPG Real Estate, Walsh, Digital Realty Bersama, Digital Connexion, Lumen, MC Digital Realty, Blackstone Frankfurt, Blackstone Paris, Medallion, Mivne and Digital Core REIT.
highlights: Fee income and other rose 98.3% in FY2025, from USD 72.5m to USD 143.8m — the fastest-growing line in the income statement
Annualised net development and management fees excluding promote income were USD 190.2m at Q2 2026; fee income grew 38% year on year on the same exclusion

The US Hyperscale Data Center Fund closed on 30 March 2026 at USD 3.25bn of equity commitments from public pensions, sovereign wealth funds, endowments, corporate pensions, insurers and family offices, targeting Northern Virginia, Santa Clara, Dallas, Atlanta, Charlotte and New York; Digital Realty holds 20% and is the manager

The Columbia Capital acquisition, announced 22 June 2026 for approximately USD 485m in 2.3 million shares with a lockup and performance earnout, brings roughly USD 9bn of fund commitments and is expected to close in the second half of 2026

The model also runs in reverse: on 29 June 2026 Digital Realty bought a blended 64% interest in three fully leased Northern Virginia data centres from Blackstone — 288 MW at a USD 7.8bn gross value and an initial stabilised cap rate above 6.5%, for USD 3.5bn in USD 1.2bn cash and USD 2.3bn of shares
Promote income now distorts the headline: Q2 2026 Core FFO was USD 2.65 a share including net promote and USD 2.13 excluding it
productsAndServices.positioning: The corpus reads this from the other side: QTS's dossier argues that unlike public REITs Digital Realty and Equinix, perpetual private capital lets a sponsor-owned landlord buy land and power years ahead of leases, and STACK's argues it prices delivery credibility without public-REIT overhead. The fund business is the answer to exactly that critique — third-party capital on a REIT's balance sheet — and no independent source assesses whether it closes the gap.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Institutional fundraising and bilateral joint ventures; Digital Core REIT is a separately listed Singapore vehicle that Digital Realty sponsors and manages.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Public pensions, sovereign wealth funds, endowments and foundations, corporate pensions, insurers, asset managers and family offices
productsAndServices.roadmap: Columbia Capital close expected in the second half of 2026, subject to regulatory approvals.

recentDevelopments.headline: Selected to develop 50 MW of new data centre capacity in Singapore
recentDevelopments.read: Singapore allocates capacity by competitive application rather than open connection; winning an allocation is a regulatory outcome, not a commercial one, and is the only route to growth in that market.

recentDevelopments.read: The same pre-emptive consent posture Compass, QTS and Vantage adopted; endorsing state standards is cheaper than fighting county by county.

recentDevelopments.read: On-ramp density is the interconnection moat; each new on-ramp raises the switching cost for hybrid-cloud tenants.

strategyRead: 1. **(High confidence)** We assess that the claim Digital Realty is the largest AI-data-centre landlord is **unfalsifiable rather than true or false**, and that the company knows it. Basis: every published ranking measures something else — Synergy measures colocation revenue share, Cushman & Wakefield ranks markets not operators, ABI Research measures active IT load, and no source ranks operators by AI-attributable leased capacity. The private platforms that a January 2026 Bank of America downgrade identified as capturing AI demand publish no comparable megawatt or revenue figure, so a category ranking would omit half the field by construction. Digital Realty's own superlative is always narrowed — 'the world's largest cloud- and carrier-neutral data center platform' — and is never attributed to a third party; the qualifier excludes hyperscaler self-build, which dwarfs both listed REITs. The defensible statement is narrower: largest by leasable area and development pipeline, second to Equinix on revenue and market value.

2. **(High confidence)** We assess the fund-management pillar is a structural response to the REIT constraint rather than a diversification play. Basis: a REIT must distribute most of its taxable income, so it cannot retain earnings to fund a USD 4.25-4.75bn annual development programme, and must issue equity and debt instead — the company issued 6.3 million shares at a weighted average USD 197.54 in June 2026 alone and a further 12.3 million for the Blackstone buy-in. Third-party capital breaks that constraint: the USD 3.25bn fund lets Digital Realty control assets on 20% of the equity while collecting a fee, and fee income rose 98.3% in FY2025. The cost is transparency — twenty unconsolidated entities now sit between the reader and the assets, and promote income has made the headline Core FFO number non-comparable to consensus.

3. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess the pre-leasing decline is a deliberate acceptance of speculative risk rather than a demand signal. Basis: capacity underway rose 82% in six months to 1,402 MW while the pre-leased share fell from 64% to 54%, meaning speculative capacity roughly doubled in absolute terms. Management simultaneously raised guidance three times and cites an 11.5% stabilised cash yield on the whole pipeline, which is only realisable if the unleased half leases. The judgment is moderate rather than high because no source establishes management intent; an equally consistent reading is that leases are lagging construction starts in a market where power, not demand, sets the schedule.

4. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess that the 2026 lease-expiry concentration is a larger near-term earnings lever than the development pipeline. Basis: 25.9% of annualised rent expires in 2026, and the greater-than-1 MW book renewed at +66.7% cash and +92.3% GAAP in Q2 2026, taking expiring rent from USD 159 to USD 265 per kW. Applied across a heavy expiry year in a supply-constrained market, mark-to-market on existing space can move earnings faster than 1,402 MW that commences over 2026-2028. Management's own guidance action is consistent — the full-year cash renewal-spread range was raised 250 basis points to 9.0-11.0%. Confidence is moderate because the 66.7% is one quarter, was attributed to APAC strength, and is not a run rate.

5. **(Moderate confidence)** We assess customer concentration is materially understated by the disclosure. Basis: the twenty largest customers are 50.9% of annualised recurring revenue and the top three approximately 26%, but nine of the twenty are redacted — including the largest at 11.7% ('Fortune 50 Software Company'), the third at 5.3% and the fourth at 4.5% — so roughly 24.6% of recurring revenue cannot be assigned to a named counterparty from public disclosure. Twenty of 310 data centres are single-customer buildings, including those occupied solely by the top three. **Collection gap:** we decline to infer the identities. No source we found resolves them, and the filing declines to say.

6. **(Low confidence)** We assess the legacy debt stack is the most underweighted risk in the equity story. Basis: USD 18.56bn of debt carries a 2.90% effective rate with a 4.5-year weighted average maturity, and USD 8.9bn matures across 2027-2029 into a materially higher rate environment; the company guided to USD 1.5-2.0bn of new long-term issuance in the second half of 2026 at 4.5-5.5%, roughly double the existing coupon. Confidence is low because no source models the earnings effect, the balance sheet is conservatively levered at 4.7 times net debt to Adjusted EBITDA with 5.2 times fixed-charge coverage, and 92% of the stack is fixed or swapped.

relationships.note: Second-largest customer at 9.0% of annualised recurring revenue across 42 locations, named in the FY2025 10-K.
relationships.context:
Oracle Corporation is the largest named customer in Digital Realty's twenty-largest-customer table — USD 424.1m of annualised recurring revenue, 9.0% of the total, across 42 locations, with a 10.2-year weighted average remaining lease term, the longest of any top-five tenant. Only the redacted 'Fortune 50 Software Company' at 11.7% is larger.

The commercial relationship runs beyond tenancy in both directions: Digital Realty deployed Oracle FastConnect in Singapore in December 2025 and announced a teaming arrangement with Oracle Solution Centers in July 2025. Oracle Cloud is one of the eight named cloud and technology alliances in the site navigation.

relationships.note: Eighth-largest customer at 1.6% of annualised recurring revenue across 49 locations, named in the FY2025 10-K.
relationships.context:
Meta Platforms, Inc. is named in the FY2025 10-K's twenty-largest-customer table at USD 73.5m of annualised recurring revenue, 1.6% of the total, spread across 49 locations with a 2.8-year weighted average remaining lease term. LinkedIn Corporation appears separately at 1.6% across 8 locations.

The location count is the interesting figure rather than the revenue: 49 sites at USD 1.5m each on average is a distributed edge and interconnection footprint, not hyperscale capacity, which Meta self-builds.

relationships.note: Named as a competitor in Digital Realty's own 10-K — and simultaneously its sixth-largest customer at 2.0% of annualised recurring revenue.
relationships.context:
Digital Realty's FY2025 10-K names Equinix first among competitors: 'We compete with numerous data center providers globally... including Equinix, Inc. and NTT'. The same filing lists Equinix as the sixth-largest customer at USD 95.6m, 2.0% of annualised recurring revenue, across 14 locations on a 4.6-year weighted average term — the clearest illustration in the corpus that colocation operators lease from each other where footprints do not overlap.

The two lead different segments and the corpus records it from Equinix's side: Equinix is the retail-segment leader at about 17% share per Synergy and leader in 16 of the top 25 metros, with Digital Realty second in North America; Equinix's dossier separately describes competing for 'the wholesale capacity Digital Realty leads'. On measurables Equinix is larger by revenue (USD 9.2bn against USD 6.11bn in FY2025) and market value, while Digital Realty is larger by net rentable area and development pipeline.

relationships.note: USD 373m supply capacity agreement for uninterruptible power supplies, low-voltage switchgear and pre-fabricated skids, announced 19 November 2025.
relationships.context:
The two companies announced a USD 373m supply capacity agreement on 19 November 2025 covering uninterruptible power supply systems, low-voltage switchgear and pre-fabricated skids. The structure is the point: this is a commitment to reserve manufacturing capacity rather than an order for equipment, which is what a buyer does when substation transformers run 75 to 110 weeks and medium-voltage switchgear is sold out into 2028.

It is the largest disclosed supplier commitment by any landlord in this corpus. Schneider's own dossier cites it as evidence that its design-led sales motion converts, while noting that no design-linked bookings figure is published and the conversion is therefore inferred.

relationships.note: Supports the NVIDIA AI Factory Research Center and the NVIDIA DSX Blueprint; holds an NVIDIA certification for a liquid-cooled data centre in Japan.
relationships.context:
Digital Realty announced support for the NVIDIA AI Factory Research Center and the NVIDIA DSX Blueprint on 3 November 2025, and debuted an NVIDIA certification for a liquid-cooled data centre in Japan on 9 February 2026. In September 2025 the two joined Oxford Quantum Circuits to launch what the parties describe as the first quantum-AI data centre in New York City.

The relationship is a specification one rather than a supply one: aligning a hall design to a reference architecture is how a landlord gets written into an AI deployment before competitive bidding. NVIDIA's dossier types its vendor relationships as partner rather than supplier for the same reason.

relationships.note: Co-founder with QTS, Vantage and Compass Datacenters of Infrastructure for America, a 501(c)(4) launched 2 September 2026 to set host-community standards.
relationships.context:
On 2 September 2026 Compass Datacenters, Digital Realty, QTS and Vantage launched Infrastructure for America, a 501(c)(4) setting host-community standards for data-centre developers. The four are direct competitors for the same hyperscale leases; the coalition is a joint response to a consent environment that has cost the industry specific projects, including the Prince William Digital Gateway that QTS and Compass lost in court.

The corpus records the coalition from Compass's side, where it sits inside a broader account of consent as a cost line. QTS's own dossier separately argues that unlike public REITs Digital Realty and Equinix, perpetual private capital lets it buy land and power years ahead of leases — so the two are allies on consent and opponents on capital structure.

relationships.note: Co-founder of the Infrastructure for America 501(c)(4) alongside Compass, Digital Realty and QTS, launched 2 September 2026.
relationships.context: Vantage Data Centers is one of the four co-founders of Infrastructure for America, announced 2 September 2026, a 501(c)(4) that sets host-community standards for data-centre developers. Vantage and Digital Realty compete directly for hyperscale capacity in Northern Virginia, Phoenix and the Nordics, and the coalition is a narrow, single-issue alliance rather than a commercial relationship.

relationships.note: Co-founder of the Infrastructure for America 501(c)(4), launched 2 September 2026; Compass was founded by a former Digital Realty executive.
relationships.context:
Compass Datacenters and Digital Realty co-founded Infrastructure for America with QTS and Vantage on 2 September 2026. Compass's dossier records the launch and quotes founder Chris Crosby — himself a former Digital Realty senior vice president — on the distinction between 'building to last and building to exit'.

The two sit at opposite ends of the ownership spectrum in this corpus: Compass is co-controlled by Brookfield Infrastructure and Ontario Teachers' with KKR at asset level and publishes no accounts, while Digital Realty publishes quarterly. An independent 2026 buyer's guide lists both, with QTS, Vantage, CyrusOne, STACK, Aligned, DataBank, NTT, Equinix xScale and Tract, as dedicated hyperscale campus developers.

relationships.note: Both are wholesale and hyperscale data-centre landlords; the contrast between them is listed-REIT against sponsor-owned capital structure.
relationships.context:
CyrusOne and Digital Realty compete for the same wholesale and hyperscale leases in Northern Virginia, Dallas, Phoenix, Chicago, Frankfurt, London, Amsterdam, Paris, Madrid and Dublin, and independent buyer's guides list them in the same set of dedicated hyperscale campus developers.

They are the cleanest listed-versus-private comparison available in this corpus. Digital Realty publishes quarterly results, a top-twenty tenant table and a development pipeline; CyrusOne, taken private by KKR and Global Infrastructure Partners in March 2022, publishes no revenue, EBITDA or backlog and reaches the capital markets through asset-backed securitisations whose collateral tables are the only public window on its tenancy. Independent rankings place them close together and disagree about the order: USDataMap's tracked-capacity table puts CyrusOne at 3,026 MW against Digital Realty's 2,878 MW, while ABI Research's active-IT-load measure puts Digital Realty at 686 MW against CyrusOne's 674 MW.

relationships.note: Digital Realty appears on DPR Construction's published colocation and wholesale client roster.
relationships.context:
DPR Construction's dossier records a named colocation and wholesale customer roster that includes Digital Realty alongside CoreSite, CyrusOne, DataBank, Equinix, Flexential, Global Switch, NTT, QTS, Stream and Vantage.

The attribution is DPR's own client list and no specific Digital Realty project, campus or contract value is named by either party. Digital Realty publishes no general-contractor relationships at all, and a Stage 2 search of industry contractor rankings found only that both companies appear in the same market listings — not that one builds for the other. The edge is recorded at the level the source supports: a builder's published client roster.

relationships.note: Three Microsoft Azure ExpressRoute cloud on-ramps deployed on the platform, announced 24 April 2025.
relationships.context:
Digital Realty announced the deployment of three Microsoft Azure ExpressRoute cloud on-ramps on 24 April 2025, and Microsoft Azure is one of eight named cloud and technology alliances in the site navigation. ExpressRoute on-ramps are the mechanism by which a colocation tenant reaches Azure over a private path rather than the public internet, and on-ramp count is one of the two numbers Digital Realty publishes for its fabric — 350-plus across 800-plus sites.

**No source establishes Microsoft as a Digital Realty tenant.** The largest customer in the FY2025 10-K is disclosed only as a 'Fortune 50 Software Company' at 11.7% of annualised recurring revenue, and the filing declines to name it; this dossier does not infer the identity.

relationships.note: Nebius's UK programme includes Digital Realty Docklands colocation, recorded on Nebius's side.
relationships.context:
The Nebius dossier records that its roughly GBP 1.7bn, approximately 65 MW-by-2027 UK programme runs across Vantage's CWL1 campus in Newport, Kao Data Harlow, the Ark Chertsey site and Digital Realty Docklands colocation.

The relationship is one-sided in the corpus: Nebius names Digital Realty as a colocation provider, and Digital Realty names no AI-cloud tenants at all. Tenant identity is redacted throughout its filings, so the neocloud side is the only place these arrangements surface.

policyExposure.regime: FERC co-location and large-load rules for PJM (Docket EL25-49)
policyExposure.exposure: FERC directed PJM on 18 December 2025, by a 5-0 vote, to create transparent rules for co-locating large loads with grid-connected generation and to revise its behind-the-meter generation rules, establishing three new transmission services: Firm Contract Demand, Non-Firm Contract Demand and Interim Non-Firm. Compliance filings were due 20 January and 16 February 2026, and FERC partially accepted and partially rejected them on 16 April 2026. Digital Realty's largest land bank sits inside PJM: the FY2025 10-K states more than 1,000 MW of developable capacity in Northern Virginia alone, and Northern Virginia carries 842 MW of white-space IT load across 32 data centres at 98.6% occupancy.
policyExposure.mitigation: None stated by the company. Digital Realty has not published a position on the docket.

policyExposure.regime: EU Energy Efficiency Directive 2023/1791 and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1364 — data-centre reporting
policyExposure.exposure: Data centres with 500 kW or more of installed IT power demand must report 24 performance indicators annually by 15 May — the 2026 deadline covered calendar 2025 — spanning energy consumption, capacity utilisation, waste heat and water, published into a European database at EU and country level. Every Digital Realty European site materially exceeds the threshold; the Interxion-legacy estate spans Frankfurt (184 MW across 29 data centres), London (96 MW), Amsterdam (140 MW), Paris, Dublin, Madrid, Marseille and the Nordics.
policyExposure.mitigation: The company reports fleet PUE of 1.38 globally and 1.31 across EMEA, WUE of 0.59, and CarbonNeutral certification covering Denmark, France, the Netherlands and Sweden — 42% of the European portfolio by IT capacity.

policyExposure.regime: Ireland — CRU large energy user connection policy and the EirGrid Dublin constraint
policyExposure.exposure: Ireland's de-facto Dublin connection moratorium, in place since 2021, was replaced in December 2025 by a policy under which new large energy users above 10 MVA must provide new on-site or proximate generation or storage, participate in the Single Electricity Market, accept mandatory demand curtailment absent performance standards, and meet 80% of annual demand from additional Irish renewable generation within six years of energisation. Digital Realty's exposure is concrete rather than prospective: its fully built DUB4 facility at Grange Castle has been reported as sitting idle awaiting grid access after two failed connection appeals.
policyExposure.mitigation: Following Ireland's July 2026 policy statement permitting private wires and on-site generation, the company was reported as intending to partner with an energy company to build its own gas plant for the Dublin site. **This is single-sourced trade-press reporting that could not be read directly** — the reporting host returned HTTP 403 and no archive capture was reachable — so the DUB4 capacity and cost figures in circulation are recorded here as unverified.

policyExposure.regime: Kansas Large Load Power Service tariff
policyExposure.exposure: The Astra Enterprise Park campus at De Soto, Johnson County, Kansas is served under the state's Large Load Power Service rate structure, and the City of De Soto's own project page states that Digital Realty will fund the transmission, substation and other electric infrastructure improvements. The same page records a 1 million gallon per day water allocation with air cooling for 85-90% of the year and evaporative cooling at peak.
policyExposure.mitigation: Self-funding the interconnection is the mitigation — the same 'pay for our own power delivery' posture EdgeCore and Compass have adopted.

policyExposure.regime: Section 232 tariffs on steel, aluminium and copper derivative articles
policyExposure.exposure: Transformers and switchgear carry a 15% rate through 31 December 2025 to 2027 under the reduced schedule for industrial and electrical grid equipment, while steel, aluminium and copper derivative articles are tariffed at 25% of full customs value. Lead times compound the cost: substation transformers at 75 to 110 weeks, generator step-up units at 100 to 150-plus weeks, and 15 kV medium-voltage switchgear at 52 to 80 weeks with many manufacturers sold out through 2028. The FY2025 10-K carries a matching risk factor on supply-chain and procurement disruption and increased supply-chain costs.
policyExposure.mitigation: The USD 373m Schneider Electric supply capacity agreement of November 2025 reserves manufacturing capacity for uninterruptible power supplies, low-voltage switchgear and pre-fabricated skids rather than ordering equipment — a direct answer to the lead-time constraint.

policyExposure.regime: US state data-centre tax exemptions under review — Virginia, Ohio, Georgia, Texas
policyExposure.exposure: Virginia's sales and use tax exemption, worth about USD 1.6bn a year against a FY2025 state and local cost of USD 1.94bn, is contested — the Senate has sought elimination or an impact fee while the House has sought environmental-compliance conditions, with fifteen data-centre bills passing in the 2026 session and no consensus reached. Ohio paused its subsidy for new applicants in May 2026 after disclosing a USD 1.6bn 2025 cost. Georgia's SB 410 would end the exemption for new data centres while grandfathering existing ones. Texas has deferred its review to the 2027 session. Digital Realty's largest US concentrations are Northern Virginia, Chicago, Dallas and Atlanta, so three of the four regimes bear directly on the portfolio.
policyExposure.mitigation: The company publicly welcomed Governor Abbott's Texas standards initiative on 7 August 2026 and co-founded the Infrastructure for America coalition on 2 September 2026 — pre-emptive engagement rather than opposition.

policyExposure.exposure: Singapore's 2019 moratorium on new data centres has been replaced by a competitive, efficiency-gated call-for-applications process rather than open connection. Digital Realty was selected to develop 50 MW of new capacity on 25 August 2026, inside a stated near-S$7bn investment programme with more than S$4.3bn for new developments.
policyExposure.mitigation: Winning an allocation is itself the mitigation; the company also opened a Global Command Center in Singapore in December 2025 and an Innovation Lab there in February 2026.

financials.commentary: Digital Realty reports as a REIT, so Core FFO per share rather than earnings per share is the number management guides and the market trades. Three consecutive guidance raises through 2026 sit against one substantive published challenge — the January 2026 Bank of America downgrade to Neutral with the price target cut to USD 170 from USD 210, arguing the pipeline is poorly located for AI demand. Two comparability warnings apply to any series built from these figures: net promote income makes Q2 2026 reported Core FFO non-comparable with consensus and with prior quarters, and the Q1 2026 consensus figure is disputed across outlets (USD 1.95 in one, USD 1.80 in another) and could not be reconciled. No published consensus was found for FY2023 or for Q2 and Q3 2025, and none has been reconstructed.
